chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Abu Jumaylah from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): If a fasting person immerses himself in water deliberately, is he required to make up that day? He said: 'He is not required to make it up, and he does not need to repeat it.'
ai.seo_question: Does deliberate full-body immersion break the fast of a fasting person?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that deliberate full-body immersion (irtimas) does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing it from eating or drinking. The phrase 'wa la ya'udanna' indicates that the person neither needs to make up the day (qada) nor repeat the fast for that specific day (i'ad), reflecting the Shia view that major impurity or immersion alone does not break the fast unless accompanied by consumption. This ruling highlights the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding what constitutes a nullifier of fasting.
